title: CaliBench: Are the Stochastic Dynamics of Video World Models Physically Calibrated?
abstract: arXiv:2608.16829v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Video world models approximate the stochastic distribution of physical outcomes through generative sampling, but existing benchmarks score individual generations or compare distributions coarsely over a whole dataset, leaving the fine-grained aleatoric uncertainty of specific phenomena untested. We introduce CaliBench, which scores outcomes in a physically interpretable discrete space - a bin index, a die face, a suit, a colour - rather than a learned feature space such as in FID, so the distance from a known reference distribution is measured directly. We curate outcome spaces whose reference is known in closed form (binomial Galton boards, Bernoulli forks, uniform dice/cards/lottery, a skewed European-roulette colour), enabling an exact calibration test. translated_title: CaliBench：视频世界模型的随机动力学是否经过物理校准？
translated_abstract: 视频世界模型通过生成采样来近似物理结果的随机分布，但现有基准测试要么对单个生成结果进行评分，要么在整个数据集上粗略地比较分布，从而未测试特定现象的细粒度偶然不确定性。我们引入了CaliBench，它在物理可解释的离散空间中对结果进行评分——例如箱索引、骰子面、花色、颜色——而不是像FID中那样使用学习到的特征空间，因此可以直接测量与已知参考分布的距离。我们构建了参考分布以闭式形式已知的结果空间（二项式高尔顿板、伯努利叉、均匀骰子/扑克牌/彩票、偏斜的欧洲轮盘颜色），从而实现精确的校准测试。我们将性能分解为两个正交轴，而单一的准确度指标会混淆它们：可评分性（生成结果可评分的比例）和校准性（生成分布与参考分布的一致性）。
tldr: CaliBench提出了一种在物理可解释离散空间中进行视频世界模型校准评估的新方法，将性能分解为可评分性和校准性两个正交维度，并利用闭式已知参考分布实现精确测试。
en_tdlr: CaliBench introduces a new approach to evaluate video world model calibration in physically interpretable discrete spaces, decomposing performance into scorability and calibration axes, with closed-form reference distributions for precise testing.
